name: High-vol-armed oversold reversion (panic snap-back)
rationale: THESIS: mean reversion only pays when vol is HIGH — elevated realized vol means price is overshooting on forced flows/liquidations, so an oversold reading is a stretched rubber band rather than the start of a calm downtrend. We buy the dip (RSI below a fitted oversold floor) ONLY when realized vol is above a fitted high-vol floor (vol_realized BOUNDED). In calm regimes oversold tends to keep grinding lower, so the vol gate is the discriminator. DISCONFIRMER: run the IDENTICAL RSI<floor rule with the vol_realized>floor gate REMOVED (bare oversold dip-buy). If vol-armed is not materially better risk-adjusted net of fees, the high-vol gate is decorative and this is just buy-the-dip. Also check: the SAME rule armed by LOW vol should be worse, proving the regime sign matters.
catalyst: Realized vol spikes above a fitted high-vol floor while RSI prints oversold — a panic flush that historically snaps back.
